name: What microfrontends solve
description: Microfrontends split a frontend along team and deployment boundaries; they trade simplicity and usually some performance for independent delivery.

name: Team and deployment coupling
description: Teams are coupled when they must coordinate to build, test and release one shared artifact.

name: Monolith, modular monolith, microfrontends
description: Three ways to structure one frontend, each with a different cost in coordination and in runtime complexity.

name: Composition techniques
description: Build-time packages, server or edge composition, iframes, web components, import maps and Module Federation are different places to join separately built parts.

name: Requirements that pick a technique
description: Independent deploy, shared state, style isolation and SEO each rule some composition techniques in or out.

name: Where Module Federation fits
description: Module Federation is one composition technique, with its own runtime, manifest and plugins; sources.md section 1 records what version 2 is.

name: Host and remote
description: A host is the application that loads modules; a remote is an application that exposes modules from its own deployment.

name: Remote loading at runtime
description: The host learns where a remote lives and fetches its entry and chunks in the browser, after the host itself has started.

name: Remote entry and manifest
description: A remote publishes a description of what it exposes and which files to fetch; the host reads it at runtime.

name: Order of requests on first load
description: The sequence of network requests on first load shows what the host knows and when.

name: Shared dependencies
description: The shared option declares which packages host and remotes should load once instead of each bundling a copy; it must be configured.

name: Duplicate React
description: Two copies of React in one page can cause an invalid hook call, because hooks resolve against the copy that renders.

name: Singleton sharing
description: A singleton share keeps one instance of a package for host and remotes.

name: requiredVersion
description: requiredVersion states which versions of a shared package a side accepts; the runtime compares it with what is available.

name: Sharing sub-paths such as react-dom/client
description: A package and its sub-path imports are separate share keys, so sharing the package alone can leave a second copy behind.

name: Contract between host and remote
description: The exposed module names, their props and their types form a contract that the host depends on without the remote knowing.

name: Types across deployments
description: Types describe the contract at build time but cannot protect a host from a remote that deployed a different shape later.

name: Versioned contracts
description: A breaking change is shipped as a new contract version while the old one stays available until consumers move.

name: Detecting a broken contract before deploy
description: A check run before release compares the new remote with what its consumers expect.

name: Who owns the URL
description: The browser has one URL, so one part of the system, usually the shell, owns it and the rest read it.

name: Nested routing across remotes
description: A shell routes to a remote by prefix and the remote routes inside that prefix.

name: Deep links into a remote
description: A URL that points inside a remote must load the shell, the remote and the right inner route on a cold start.

name: Communication without shared code
description: Parts can talk through custom events, URL state and props callbacks without importing each other.

name: A shared store couples deploys
description: A store shared by several remotes becomes a contract: changing its shape forces coordinated releases.

name: Custom events
description: The browser dispatches and listens to named events on the page, which needs no import between publisher and subscriber.

name: URL as shared state
description: State kept in the URL is readable by every part and survives reloads and links.

name: Global scope of CSS
description: A stylesheet applies to the whole document unless something scopes it, so a rule in one remote can restyle another.

name: Style isolation options and costs
description: Naming conventions, scoped CSS and shadow DOM isolate styles at different costs; none is free.

name: Shadow DOM as isolation
description: Shadow DOM gives a component its own style scope, with limits on how outside styles reach it.

name: Independent deployment
description: Each remote is built and released alone, and the host finds its current version at runtime.

name: Remote URLs per environment
description: The host needs a different address for each remote in development, staging and production.

name: Cache busting
description: A new release must reach the browser even when an older entry file is cached.

name: Rolling back one remote
description: Rolling back a remote restores an earlier build without redeploying the host or other remotes.

name: When a remote is down
description: A remote that fails to load is a runtime event the host must handle, or the failure spreads.

name: Performance cost of splitting
description: Splitting adds requests, duplicate code and chained loading that a single bundle does not have.

name: Waterfall loading
description: When one request can start only after another finishes, delays add up.

name: Preloading
description: Telling the browser early which files will be needed moves requests earlier in the sequence.
